idiom_name: constant Hash of lambdas (or classes) keyed by Symbol
implementation_notes: Ruby needs no structure beyond a Hash: a constant REGISTRY mapping keys to lambdas, a register(name, callable = nil, &block) that stores either a Proc or a class, and a create(name) that uses Hash#fetch with a block so an unknown key raises instead of returning nil. Builders are closures, so constructor arguments are captured at registration time, and storing the class itself lets create send .new when the constructor needs no arguments. What replaces the classic structure: Hash plus Proc - one factory class per product would be pure ceremony - and Object.const_get provides the reflective shortcut when a key must resolve to a class name, walking ::-qualified paths and raising NameError on an unknown constant. Freeze the registry after configuration and give tests a reset hook, because a constant table is process-wide.
pitfalls: A constant Hash is process-wide and mutable: registrations from one test leak into the next unless the kit offers reset, or each component gets its own registry object.
Hash#[] returns nil for a missing key, so a typo surfaces later as a NoMethodError on nil - use fetch with a block and raise a named error.
Object.const_get accepts arbitrary strings (including ::-paths) and will resolve any constant in the process, so never feed it user input - look keys up in the registry instead.
